oneOf.description: The frame is not JSON, not text, or not a known handshake request.
No frame arrived within the handshake deadline.

Wrong, expired, exhausted or already used pairing secret. The cases
are deliberately indistinguishable.
Too many failed pairing attempts on this host; see `retry_after_secs`.
Unknown device, revoked device or wrong token; indistinguishable.

A retired refresh token was presented: a copy of the device's key was
used, and the whole pairing was revoked. Pair again if this was you.

The access token has expired or was replaced. The pairing is still
valid: authenticate with the refresh token instead.
The authenticated device cannot perform this operation.
The gateway is at its connection or device limit.

The host holds as many connection requests as it takes, or this
address already has one open. Retry later.
This address was denied a moment ago; see `retry_after_secs`.
The device was revoked while connected. Do not reconnect.
The device did not read fast enough and its queue overflowed.
Nothing was received from the device for too long.

Sent only by a gateway without session routing; kept for
compatibility.

HostRoute.description: One address a device can dial this host at, as the handshake reports it.

provider.description:
Which mesh product the address is on, when the interface name says:
`netbird`, `tailscale` or `zerotier`. Absent for a LAN address and for
a tunnel whose name names no product (macOS's `utunN`).

HostRouteKind.description:
How a device reaches this host over one route. A gateway reports each
address it answers on with the kind of network it is on.

oneOf.description: A private IPv4 address on a local network interface (Wi-Fi, Ethernet).

A private overlay or VPN address: a `100.64.0.0/10` mesh address, or a
tunnel-facing unique-local address on a tunnel interface. `vpn` is
what a gateway before this kind reported and is still read.
A host name: the machine's `.local` name, or another advertised name.

A public address or name. Plain LAN traffic is unencrypted, so a
client should prefer the other kinds.

OverlayProvider.description:
The mesh product an interface belongs to, when its name says which one.
macOS names every VPN `utunN`, so there the provider stays unknown and the
address is reported as a plain overlay address.

Secret.description:
A pairing credential, manual code or device token. Serializes as a plain
string; `Debug` never prints the value, so it cannot reach logs or error
strings through a derived impl.

description:
Frames the gateway sends during the handshake, and the error frame that
precedes a close. After authentication an `error` frame is never the
answer to a request: those are `response` frames carrying the request ID.

oneOf.description:
The answer to `describe`: who this gateway is, and nothing secret. The
socket stays open for the next first frame.

capabilities.description:
What this gateway takes beyond protocol v1's first frames:
[`GATEWAY_CAPABILITY_DESCRIBE`], [`GATEWAY_CAPABILITY_MACHINE_CODES`].

host_name.description: The host's own name, for display. A label, not an identity.

version.description: The RustCode version running on this host.

oneOf.description:
The connection request is in front of the host's owner. Wait on the
same socket, sending nothing but pings, for the answer.

expires_in_secs.description: Time the owner has to answer.

oneOf.description:
The owner accepted and the host shows a code. Send one `pair` frame
with `method: "code"` and that code within `expires_in_secs`. Only
this socket can redeem it.

code_length.description: Digits in the code, without its separator.

oneOf.description: The owner denied the request. The connection closes.

Nobody answered in time, the code was not sent in time, or a newer
code on the host replaced it. The connection closes; ask again.

Pairing succeeded. `token` is shown exactly once, or, for a device that
asked for `token_rotation`, `refresh_token` and `access_token` are; the
connection is authenticated as this device from here on.

access_expires_at.description:
When `access_token` stops being accepted, RFC 3339 in UTC; the
device then authenticates with its refresh token.

access_token.description: The access token to reconnect with, until `access_expires_at`.

expires_at.description:
When this pairing stops being accepted, RFC 3339 in UTC. The device
pairs again after it. Absent for a device that rotates its tokens:
its pairing lasts until it is revoked.

host_name.description: The host's own name, for display. A label, not an identity.

platform.description:
What this host runs: `macos`, `linux` or `windows`. The device's
machine list shows it; absent from an older host, whose platform
stays `unknown`.

refresh_token.description:
The rotating device's first refresh token; shown exactly once and
stored durably.

routes.description:
The addresses this host answers on right now, best first: its LAN
addresses, a mesh VPN (`100.64.0.0/10`) address and its `.local`
name. A device adds them to the routes it knows for this host, so
pairing once is enough to reach it on another network. Absent from
an older gateway and when the listener is loopback only.

token.description:
The static device token of a device that does not rotate; shown
exactly once. Absent for a device that rotates its tokens.

version.description:
The RustCode version running on this host, so the app can say which
machine needs updating. A label for the owner, never a protocol
gate; absent from an older host.

wire_names.description:
`"thread"` when the gateway accepted the device's request for the
thread names; absent means the v1 names.

oneOf.description:
The device token was accepted, or, for a rotating device, the access
token or refresh token it presented was.

access_expires_at.description: When the access token stops being accepted, RFC 3339 in UTC.

access_token.description: The access token for this connection, until `access_expires_at`.

expires_at.description:
When this pairing stops being accepted, RFC 3339 in UTC. The device
pairs again after it. Absent for a device that rotates its tokens.

platform.description: What this host runs, as in `paired`.

refresh_token.description:
The new refresh token, when the device presented a refresh token.
Replace the stored one and answer with `token_ack`.

rotation_id.description:
Identifies this rotation, to acknowledge with `token_ack`. Absent
when nothing rotated: an access token reconnected.

routes.description: The addresses this host answers on right now, as in `paired`.

version.description: The RustCode version running on this host, as in `paired`.

wire_names.description:
`"thread"` when the gateway accepted the device's request for the
thread names; absent means the v1 names.

supported_versions.description:
Set with [`ErrorCode::UnsupportedVersion`]: the handshake versions
this gateway speaks, so the device can say which one to update to.
